comments.text:
I'm an artist. I know the grind to have a skill you worked hard for. But the nature of it is that individual art with haircuts doesn't have any scale like other reproductive arts might [brand deals, games, films, etc.]. 
People *will* pay for great work, but there's only so many people in an area that can afford that. Most of the time, people just need "acceptable" for $25 tops, which should be roughly 20-30 mins of your time as a barber. That means a gross rate of $50 an hour if you run your own operation, then you take the expenses out, and it will be a little less, but not by a lot. Rent and utility will be the main cost for a business with little to no supply needs. After everything is said and done, you're probably being paid around 60k annually with wiggle room for working faster or having others join you in a busy area. That's not crazy money, but I know VFX artists & Asset developers in the tech sector getting paid the same rate who also went to college for that. It is much more comfortable than minimum wage though, and I know tons of people that aren't even getting that. 
Realistically, I would wish they got paid more, but the entire economy is being screwed over and it grinds everything to a halt.
